GENERAL DESCRIPTION
Omar Rene Espinoza Navarro. RUT: 5.831.904-K, Chilean nationality, is a professor of Biology and Natural Sciences from the University of Chile, Master in Education from the University of Tarapacá and PhD in Cellular Biology and Genetics, obtained at the Autonomous University of Madrid, Spain. Diplomat in Ethics of Scientific Research (Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile) and postgraduate courses in Ethics of Good Clinical Practices (Universidad de Chile-Santiago).
Full Professor at the University of Tarapacá, Department of Biology, Faculty of Sciences. The lines of research development are related to: Reproductive Biology, Environmental Pollution, Human Morphometry and Ethics of Scientific investigation.
Participated in innumerable national and international congresses in the presentation of his professional work, which is reflected in his scientific productivity with more than 50 publications in WOS (ISI) impact specialty journals.
Is a Peer Evaluator of Undergraduate Careers and Doctoral Program in Agencies: CNA, Engineering SA, AcreditaAcción, Qualitas. He participates as Director in associations scientific organizations such as: Sociedad Chilena de Anatomía; Sociedad Panamericana de Anatomía; Sociedad Chilena de Reproducción y Desarrollo; Sociedad Chilena de Ciencias del Movimiento.
Member of the Academic Committee (CAP) of the Master's in Public Health and Master's in  Sciences of the Physical activity.
From 2010 to date he is President of the Ethics / Bioethics Committee of the University of Tarapacá (2010 – 2016) and then President of the Accredited Scientific Ethics Committee (CEC-UTA), achieving his second accreditation for three years (2021-2024).
In teaching, is the chairs of Biology and Physiology for the Careers of Education and in Health Sciences. In Linkage with the Environment, he is Project Coordinator for Teaching of Morphological Sciences in conjunction with the Chilean Society of Anatomy, updating scientific concepts and creating links between university academics National and international.
Participate actively in the creation of human resources in the theses supervision of the Graduate Programs.

0000-0003-4885-9714.bio:
Leonardo Figueroa-Tagle ha dedicado su vida a la química y a la enseñanza, convirtiéndose en una figura clave dentro de la Universidad de Tarapacá, donde ejercio desde 1982 hasta 2025, como profesor asociado en el Departamento de Química. Su vocación lo ha llevado a combinar la docencia con la investigación, siempre con un fuerte compromiso hacia la sostenibilidad y el cuidado del medio ambiente.

Desde sus primeros pasos como laboratorista químico, Leonardo mostró un interés profundo por comprender cómo los procesos químicos se relacionan con la salud, el clima y los ecosistemas. Esa curiosidad se transformó en una carrera académica marcada por la producción científica: más de una cuarenta publicaciones, más de 90 presentaciones en congresos nacionales e internacionales,  que abordan problemáticas actuales y buscan soluciones prácticas para mejorar la calidad de vida y proteger nuestro entorno.

Su trabajo no se limita a los laboratorios ni a las aulas. Leonardo se ha vinculado con los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible de la ONU, aportando en áreas tan relevantes como la salud y el bienestar, la acción por el clima y la protección de la vida submarina. Esta conexión refleja su visión de la ciencia como una herramienta para transformar la sociedad y enfrentar los grandes desafíos globales.

Más allá de los artículos y proyectos, quienes lo conocen destacan su capacidad para inspirar a estudiantes y colegas. Su biografía es la historia de un académico que entiende la química no solo como una disciplina científica, sino como un puente hacia un futuro más responsable y consciente con el planeta.

0000-0002-7141-2710.bio:
Claudio González is Chilean, married. He is a Doctor of Science from the University of Chile. He with PostDoctoral stay in molecular electronics and Biomass at the same University. He is a ex Full Professor at the University of Tarapacá. He was a former Professor of Physics at the Metropolitan Technological University. Former Professor of Chemistry at the University of Chile. He has taught Mechanics, Electromagnetism, Optics and Waves and Instrumental Analysis in the first and General Chemistry, Physicochemistry, Introduction to Environmental Sciences, Environmental Chemistry. Atmospheric Chemistry in the second. He has also worked as a Professor at the Professional Institute of the Chilean Security Association, the DUOC-UC Professional Institute and the Valle Central Professional Institute. He has ten years of academic experience in the area of Atmospheric Chemistry and Environmental Chemistry, ten years of experience in General Chemistry from the Baccalaureate Program of the University of Chile, twenty years of experience in Applied Physical Chemistry in various Professional Institutes and three years of experience. in Mechanics, Electromagnetism and Optics and Waves.
Environmental Research is being developed. In the environmental area, he has fifteen years of Research in Environmental Physicochemistry on the subject of predictive mathematical models of critical episodes of air pollution by particulate matter in the Metropolitan Region, based on the design of meteorological indicators for these models. And fifteen years in particulate matter modeling using US EPA codes such as SCREEN3©, simulating the movement of MP10 type particulate matter, according to data from weather stations and the AP-42 standard, in a 3D topographic projection using Digitized maps indicating the areas of influence of the particulate material, according to the Chilean standard. He also performs air pollution studies using other open sources such as OpenAir ©, ALOHA © and HYSPLIT ©. He has designed and developed several Environmental Physics and Chemistry Laboratories: for example, evaluation of UV and Visible radiation and use of the solar chart. His interests are to investigate ozone concentration in the troposphere and stratosphere by optical spectroscopy based on two-frequency laser irradiation, characterization of the thermal inversion layer over the Metropolitan Region basin, and the analysis of polluting gases by differential optical absorption.
He has also worked in the ENERGY area formulating R+D+i Projects. He has presented Projects at INNOVA CORFO for the production of Biodiesel, Domeyko Projects for the Vice-Rector for Research and Development of the University of Chile related to the conversion of biomass to energy in Evaluation of Energy Platforms using Biomass, formation of ENAP-U Consortiums. of Chile for the manufacture of biodiesel from lignocellulosic materials, Projects for the IDB in energy efficiency and technological innovation and several tenders for Biomass studies, Cadastre of Renewable Energy Sources, all of them for the National Energy Commission (through the ChileCompras portal ) as Consultant and Industrial Pre-evaluations for the Company BIODIESEL Chile in its pilot plant located in the commune of Lo Espejo, RM.
He has worked as an Air Quality Consultant for Pampa Camarones S.A, Somarco Ltda. COMSA de Chile S.A and Compañía Minera Los Pelambres on behalf of GESCAM Gestión de la Calidad Ambiental S.A, as Scientific Advisor of the National Center for the Environment, Associate Researcher of the Center of Environmental Chemistry of the University of Chile and of the Soil-Plant-Water Laboratory of the same University, Academic Coordinator of the Diploma in Environmental Sciences of the University of Chile, Researcher of the Chilean Nuclear Energy Commission, Advisor of several FONDECYT Projects. As a reviewer member of Thesis for the University of Chile, the University of Antioquia Colombia and the Catholic University of the Santísima Concepción. As Referee of the Atmospheric Pollution and Aerosol and Air Quality Research Magazines. As Sponsor Professor of Thesis for the Universidad Tecnológica Metropolitana, and as Scientific Evaluator of Projects of the EXPLORA Program of CONICYT. Academic Collaborator of the 2007 Energy Workshop organized by the Vice-Rector for Research and Development of the University of Chile. Recording Secretary of the Domeyko Program of the same Vice-Rectory. He has also completed a Diploma in Environmental Sciences.
He has twenty years of experience in research in physical chemistry of materials and more than thirty years of experience in university teaching. He has published various papers in Materials Physicochemistry, Materials Engineering, Molecular Photophysics, Organometallic Synthesis and Atmospheric Sciences..
His skills are research, strategic planning, teamwork, goal and achievement oriented, and teacher evaluation.

0000-0001-9250-6102.bio:
Mi formación académica ha sido guiada por un compromiso constante con el estudio de los fenómenos psicosociales en contextos comunitarios y educativos. Inicié mi camino profesional obteniendo el grado de Licenciado en Psicología por la Universidad de Tarapacá (2004), donde desarrollé las bases teóricas y prácticas para comprender las dinámicas individuales y colectivas en entornos complejos.

Consolidando este interés, cursé el Magíster en Psicología Educacional en la misma universidad (2009), especializándome en intervenciones psicosociales en contextos escolares y comunitarios del norte de Chile. Esta etapa me permitió integrar herramientas para abordar problemáticas como la exclusión educativa y la construcción de identidad en espacios multiculturales.

Para profundizar en el análisis crítico de las dinámicas sociales, realicé un Doctorado en Ciencias Sociales y del Comportamiento en la Universidad de A Coruña, España. Durante esta formación, investigué procesos de apropiación del espacio en comunidades urbanas, lo que enriqueció mi perspectiva teórica y metodológica con enfoques internacionales, siempre manteniendo un fuerte vínculo con las realidades locales.

Esta trayectoria académica, desde la psicología educacional hasta las ciencias sociales, refleja mi vocación por investigar e intervenir en problemáticas psicosociales con rigor científico y sensibilidad comunitaria, siempre orientado a generar conocimientos útiles para la transformación social.

Mi carrera como académico e investigador se ha desarrollado principalmente en la Universidad de Tarapacá, sede Iquique, donde me he desempeñado como instructor en el Departamento de Ciencias Sociales desde marzo de 2015 hasta la actualidad. En esta institución, he combinado labores de docencia e investigación, con especial énfasis en el área psicosocial y comunitaria.

Previamente, entre agosto de 2006 y diciembre de 2014, formé parte del cuerpo docente de la Carrera de Psicología en la misma universidad, donde impartí diversas asignaturas fundamentales para la formación profesional en psicología comunitaria. 

Paralelamente, entre abril de 2010 y julio de 2013, contribuí a la formación de psicólogos en la Universidad Arturo Prat, específicamente en su Departamento de Ciencias Sociales.

Esta amplia experiencia en diversas instituciones de educación superior me ha permitido desarrollar un enfoque integral de la psicología, combinando perspectivas teóricas con aplicaciones prácticas, especialmente en el ámbito comunitario y de intervención social. Mi labor se ha centrado particularmente en contextos del norte de Chile, lo que ha enriquecido mi comprensión de las particularidades psicosociales de esta región.

I am currently a Serra Hunter Fellow  at the UAB in Barcelona and a Senior Research fellow at the Universidad de Tarapacá (Chile). Recently, I was a full Professor of Higher Education at the Faculty of Education and Humanities at the Universidad de Tarapacá (Chile), in which capacity I have been the principal investigator (and leader) of various national research projects.  

I am also simultaneously  an Honorary Supervisor at the EdD Programme in Higher Education at the University of Liverpool (UK).

I am interested in the study of higher education.  Initially, I focused my work on (i) the study university teaching-learning processes and (ii) academic identities. For the last few years, I have been conducting research on (iii) the role of the universities in the twenty-first century and their relationship to the state, (iv) the public/private divide in universities, and (v) the decolonisation of universities.

All my research is conducted within a global horizon and much of it is explicitly comparative and critical in character. Wherever practicable, my work contains an examination of systems and processes in different countries, and I seek to develop theoretical frameworks that have cross-national application.

0000-0002-6487-8096.bio:
David Laroze is a Full Professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies at the University of Tarapacá (Chile), where he holds the Chair of Mathematical Modeling. He was the Director of the Institute for several years. Previously, he served as a Visiting Professor at Universidad de Navarra (Spain), a Research Associate at the Physics and Astronomy School at the University of Glasgow (United Kingdom), a Postdoctoral Researcher at the Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research (Germany) and the University of Chile, and an Assistant Professor at the Pontifical Catholic University of Valparaiso. He holds a Ph.D. in Physics from the Federico Santa Maria Technical University and joined the CMS collaboration in 2022, in which he was among the winners of the 2025 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics for being a member of the collaboration.

He has published more than 420 papers in journals indexed in the Web of Science – Journal Citation Reports, including Nature, Reports on Progress in Physics, Physical Review Letters, Physical Review B, Physical Review E, Physical Review D, Macromolecules, Scientific Reports, Applied Physics Letters, Nanotechnology, Organic Electronics, Journal of Chemical Physics, Communication in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulations, Chaos, Nonlinear Dynamics, International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer, PLB, PLA, Photochemical and Photobiological Sciences, Physics of Fluids, Atmospheric Research, and the Journal of High Energy Physics, among others. In 2024, he was selected as one of the World's Top 2% Scientists, published by Stanford University and Elsevier.

He has advised numerous undergraduate and Ph.D. students and has mentored postdoctoral researchers. Additionally, he has participated in both scientific and organizing committees of various conferences and serves as a reviewer for many international journals. His current research interests include nonlinear phenomena, magnetism, hydrodynamic instabilities, radiation issues, and thermal and electronic transport in quantum systems, as well as high energy physics.

0000-0003-4262-3786.bio:
Manuel Prieto received his Ph.D. in Geography from The University of Arizona. He is a professor in the Department of Historical and Geographical Sciences at the Universidad de Tarapacá (Arica, Chile). He serves as Director of the Millennium Nucleus in Andean Peatlands (AndesPeat), principal investigator of the Anillos project "Geopolitics of Lithium Off-sites: Infrastructures, Territories, and Ecologies" (LiOness), and research associate at the Center for Intercultural and Indigenous Research (ciir.cl).
He positions his work within critical physical geography, an emergent field in human-environment geography that integrates critical social theory with environmental science to understand how socio-political power and biophysical processes together shape landscapes, environmental change, and unequal exposures to harm. His approach combines qualitative and quantitative methods to examine both the material and political dimensions of socio-environmental change.  His current work focuses on the socio-ecological transformations of high Andean wetlands and agricultural valleys in the Atacama Desert, exploring how these landscapes are shaped by climate change, cultural water management, and mining activities. He also leads research projects that examine the presence, distribution, and social impacts of toxic metal contamination associated with mining operations in these regions.

0000-0002-4893-0050.bio: Mónica Meza Aliaga is a geographer and professor at the Department of Historical and Geographic Sciences at the University of Tarapacá in Chile. She is also principal researcher of the Millennium Nucleus in Andean Peatlands (AndesPeat), where she contributes to the line of research on Forms of Knowledge. She has a Doctor in Geography (2021) from the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile. Her research has covered various interests linked to strategic ecological resources such as soil, problematizing use and management practices that under the prevailing economic rationality have impacted the sustainability and environmental functions of this resource. Practices of adaptation to climate variability developed in the past by indigenous communities in northern Chile and the understanding of the social production of the Andean territory of northern Chile, based on geographical imaginaries that explain the notion of depopulation and emptiness of the mountain range of Arica. Her work has been funded by the Chilean National Research and Development Agency (ANID) and the University of Tarapacá.

0000-0002-3201-6790.bio:
I currently serve as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Physics at the Universidad de Tarapacá, Chile. My research is primarily focused on nonlinear physics, statistical mechanics, complex systems, agent-based modeling, and higher education studies.

My main research line seeks to understand and model complex dynamics in physical and educational systems using advanced statistical methods and numerical simulations. In recent years, I have been actively involved in projects focused on the quantitative analysis of student academic workload using digital platforms, as well as the development of statistical models for adaptive curriculum redesign based on student performance indicators.

I'm co-investigator of the Fondecyt Regular, Nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation and its connecion with nonaditive entropic measures describing complex systems, GRANT NUMBER: 1240810,years 2024–2028, Main researcher of UTA Mayor project, Dynamics and Thermodynamics of the d-HMF Model with External Magnetic Field, GRANT NUMBER: 0.080/2023, year 2023.

Additionally I'm co-investigator of Spain projects:

- Impact of curriculum design on the performance quality indices of the degrees of the Higher Technical School of Design Engineering (ETSID), Universitat Politecnica de Valencia, GRANT NUMBER: UPV-PIME-I-1930/2023, years 2023-2025.
- Quantitative methods for estimating academic credits and quality indices, Universidad de Sevilla, GRANT NUMBER: US-III.3A-2023-03-24, years 2023-2024
- Development of methods and tools for Curriculum Analysis for the study of university degrees in the European Higher Education Area, Universidad de Sevilla, GRANT NUMBER:US-III.3A-2025-03-06, years  2025-2028.

I was investigator of UCN-DGPRE project GRANT NUMBER: 040/2021, What Are Our Students Doing? Reconstructing Academic Workload in Remote Learning through Digital Platform Records.  Additionally, I have led an educational innovation project funded by FDPD (2019), focused on implementing active learning strategies in introductory physics courses.

My recent publications address topics such as quasi-stationary states in systems with long-range interactions, complexity measures applied to these systems, generalized statistical distributions in physics, and data-driven methodologies for evaluating academic performance in higher education.

0000-0002-3771-4694.bio: Dr. Saravanan Rajendran is currently working as a Professor in the IAI, University of Tarapacá, Arica, Chile, and. also as Research Associate in SERC, University of Chile, and Santiago, Chile. He received his PhD in Physics – Material Science in 2013 from the Department of Nuclear Physics, University of Madras, Chennai, India. He was awarded the University Research Fellowship (URF) during the years 2009–2011 by the University of Madras. After working as an Assistant Professor at Dhanalakshmi College of Engineering, Chennai, India, from 2013 to 2014, he was awarded SERC and CONICYT-FONDECYT postdoctoral fellowship by the University of Chile, Santiago, Chile, in 2014–2017. He has worked (2017–2018) in the research group of Professor John Irvine, School of Chemistry, University of St Andrews, UK, as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow within the framework of a EPSRC-Global Challenges Research Fund for the removal of Blue-Green Algae and their toxins. He is Associate Editor of International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology (Springer). Also, Editorial Member and Guest Editor of several reputed journals. Currently, He is handling several project FONDECYT, FONDAP, UTAMAYOR and etc., His research interests focus in the area of nanostructured functional materials, photophysics, surface chemistry and nanocatalysts for renewable energy and wastewater purification. He has published in 170+ (10900+ citation and h index 46) international peer-reviewed journals and 20+ book chapters and edited 13+ books for renowned international Publishers. He was awarded 2% top scientists by Stanford University researchers, USA for the last three years continuously. Further, recently his name was in the list of Top 1% world scientist by Clarivate (WOS).based citations.
